title: Non-destructive Barcoding of Freshwater Macroinvertebrates with MinION
author: Elise C. Knobloch
materials: Let sit for 00:10:00 at room temperature
Qubit Fluorometer (Quantas TM Fluorometer protocol listed below)
Quantify Following same quantifying protocol as previously listed
View resulting CO1 sequences for further analyses.

steps.title: Prepare Specimens and Plate
steps.instruction: Prepare specimens for DNA extraction using a 96-well plate.

substeps.instruction: Fill two Petri dishes with ddH2O.
Remove specimens from ethanol and place in one dish of ddH2O for 00:10:00 (use a microscope if necessary).
Remove specimens from water and rinse in the second dish for 00:05:00.
Place specimens on a paper towel to dry for approximately 00:05:00, arranging them in rows of eight.
Add 10 µL QuickExtract DNA Extraction Solution (Lucigen Catalog #QE09050) to each well of a 96-well plate (working in rows of three is recommended).

Place one rinsed and dried specimen head-first in each well, ensuring the head is fully submerged. If the specimen is too large, remove a leg and place it in the extract, keeping one side of the specimen intact.

steps.title: Extract DNA
steps.instruction: Perform heat-based DNA extraction and transfer the extract.

substeps.instruction: Cover the 96-well plate with TempPlate sealing foil or a reusable TempPlate pressure-fit sealing mat.
Place the covered plate in a thermal cycler and heat at 65 °C for 00:18:00, then at 98 °C for 00:02:00.
Carefully remove the QuickExtract DNA Extraction Solution from each well and transfer it to a clean 96-well plate, avoiding contact with the specimens.
If a well contains no liquid due to specimen absorption, add 10 µL of ddH2O, pipette up and down, and remove this as the extract.

steps.title: Dilute DNA Extracts
steps.instruction: Dilute the extracted DNA to a generalized concentration for PCR.

substeps.instruction: Put 10 µL of ddH2O in each well of a new 96-well plate.
Add 1 µL of DNA extraction to each coinciding well (1:10 dilution).
Seal the dilution plates well to prevent evaporation during storage.

steps.title: Prepare PCR Master Mix
steps.instruction: Prepare a master mix for the PCR reactions.

substeps.instruction: Combine ddH2O, 2.0X Taq RED Master Mix (Genesee Scientific Catalog #42-138), and the specific forward primer in a tube.
For a single 20 µL reaction: 7 µL H2O, 10 µL 2x Buffer-APEX red, 0.5 µL Primer F (Primer R and DNA Template are added separately).
For a 25x master mix: 175 µL H2O, 250 µL 2x Buffer-APEX red, 12.5 µL Primer F.

steps.title: Set Up PCR Reactions
steps.instruction: Distribute master mix and add specimen-specific components on ice.

substeps.instruction: Vortex and spin down the 25x master mix.
Distribute 17.5 µL of master mix into each tube of a strip tube on an ice block.
Add 0.5 µL of a unique reverse primer and 2 µL of a unique specimen's diluted DNA to each tube.

steps.title: Run PCR Amplification
steps.instruction: Amplify the DNA using a T100 Thermal Cycler (BioRad, 1861096).

substeps.instruction: Initial denaturation: 94 °C for 00:01:00.
Final extension: 72 °C for 00:07:00.
Hold: Infinite hold at 10 °C.

steps.title: Verify and Pool PCR Products
steps.instruction: Confirm amplification via gel electrophoresis and pool the products.

substeps.instruction: Run a gel on at least 6 specimens from each master mix batch to estimate success rate.
Take 4 µL from each PCR reaction to create a pooled PCR product (approximately 1.152 mL total).

steps.title: Purify Pooled PCR Product
steps.instruction: Clean the pooled PCR product using AMPure XP beads.

substeps.instruction: Take 250 µL of the pooled PCR and add 125 µL of 0.5 X AMPure XP beads (Beckman Coulter Catalog #A63880); pipette up and down to mix.
Place on a magnetic rack for 00:02:00 with the tube open.
Remove supernatant, leaving approximately 5 µL at the bottom.
Add 250 µL of freshly made 70% ethanol, pipette gently up and down, and remove all ethanol.
Add another 250 µL of 70% ethanol and let sit for 00:00:30, then remove all ethanol.
Let dry with the cap open for 00:05:00 to 00:10:00.
Add 40 µL of ddH2O to elute the pellet; remove from rack.
Return to rack to form a pellet, remove the liquid, and transfer the purified product to a clean tube.
Verify purity via gel electrophoresis (successful if no bands appear below the Co1 band).

steps.title: Quantify and Dilute DNA
steps.instruction: Quantify the cleaned PCR product and dilute to the required concentration.

substeps.instruction: Quantify using a Quantas Fluorometer (Promega, E6150): Mix 1 µL DNA with 200 µL QuantiFluor ONE dsDNA Dye in a 0.5ml tube, vortex, and read.
Dilute DNA to a concentration of 100-200 fmol amplicon DNA.
Example dilutions: If 41 ng/µL, use 1.5 µL DNA and 21 µL water; if 80-94 ng/µL, use 1 µL DNA and 21.5 µL water.

steps.title: End Repair and Size Selection
steps.instruction: Perform end repair and clean the DNA library.

substeps.instruction: Combine in a strip-tube: 22.5 µL diluted DNA, 3.5 µL NEBNext Ultra II End Prep Reaction Buffer (NEB Catalog #E7647), 1.5 µL NEBNext Ultra II End Prep Enzyme Mix (NEB Catalog #E7646), and 2.5 µL H2O.
Heat at 20 °C for 00:05:00, then 65 °C for 00:05:00.
Transfer the mix into a new 1.5 ml tube.
Add 30 µL of vortexed AMPure XP beads to the mixture.
Incubate on a Hula mixer for 00:05:00.
Spin down and place on a magnet until clear; pipette off the supernatant.
Add 100 µL of 70% ethanol (do not touch pellet) and remove ethanol.
Add another 100 µL of 70% ethanol, spin down, return to magnetic rack, and remove ethanol.
Allow to dry for 00:00:30.
Add 30.5 µL of ddH2O, remove from rack, and resuspend pellet.
Incubate off rack for 00:02:00, then place back on rack until clear.
Remove liquid and transfer to a clean tube.

steps.title: Ligation and Final Cleanup
steps.instruction: Ligate adapters and perform final purification of the library.

substeps.instruction: Prepare reagents on ice: Spin down Adapter Mix (AMX) and NEBNext Quick T4 DNA Ligase; thaw and vortex Ligation Buffer (LNB), Elution Buffer (EB), and Short Fragment Buffer (SFB).
Combine in a new tube: 30 µL DNA from previous step, 12.5 µL LNB, 5 µL NEBNext Quick T4 DNA Ligase, and 2.5 µL AMX.
Flick, spin, and incubate at room temperature for 00:10:00.
Add 20 µL of vortexed AMPure XP beads, flick, and incubate on a Hula mixer at room temperature for 00:05:00.
Spin, place on magnetic rack, let pellet form, and pipette off supernatant.
Add 125 µL of SFB, flick to resuspend, spin down, return to rack, and remove supernatant. Repeat this SFB wash step once more.
Add 15 µL of EB, spin down, resuspend, and incubate at room temperature for 00:10:00.
Place on magnetic rack, allow pellet to form, and transfer liquid to a clean tube (repeat twice for full cleaning).

steps.title: Final Library Dilution and Priming
steps.instruction: Dilute the final library and prime the flow cell.

substeps.instruction: Dilute the DNA library to a concentration of 3-20 fmol (e.g., if 1.2 ng/µL, use 3 µL DNA and 2 µL EB; if 1.4 ng/µL, use 2.9 µL DNA and 2.2 µL EB).
Prepare priming buffer: Mix 117 µL Flush Buffer (FB) and 3 µL Flush Tether (FLT) (ONT Catalog #EXP-FLP002).
Insert 120 µL priming buffer into the flow cell.
Prepare DNA library mix: Mix 15 µL of 10 µL Sequencing Buffer II (SBII), 10 µL Loading Beads II (LBII), and 5 µL DNA library.
Insert 30 µL of the prepped DNA library into the flow cell.

steps.title: Sequencing and Data Processing
steps.instruction: Run the sequencing and process the resulting data.

substeps.instruction: Set sequencing parameters: Kit SQK-LSK-109, run time of 17 hours, and disable FastQ compression.
Create an Excel sheet with 5 columns: sample/specimen ID, forward tag, reverse tag, forward primer sequence, and reverse primer sequence (ensure no extra spaces/punctuation).
Save the demultiplexing information as a .txt file.
Merge resulting Fastq files using MergeFasta.
Run ONTBarcoder using default parameters.
